newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea seeks arrest of aides to president's son.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea seeks arrest of aides to president's son.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors said on Wednesday they were seeking arrest warrants for close associates of President Kim Young-sam's son.
"The prosecution has asked a Seoul criminal court to issue warrants to arrest Mr Kim Hi-chan and Mr Park Tae-joong," a prosecution official said.

The official, who declined to be identified, said the two would be charged with taking bribes in return for promises to ask the president's second son, Kim Hyun-chul, for help in obtaining government licences for broadcasting and other projects.
Hundreds of millions of won (hundreds of thousands of dollars) were involved, he said, without giving details.

Separately, state radio said prosecutors had found evidence that Kim Hyun-chul had accepted 300 million won ($336,000) from a local company. The prosecution official declined to comment on the report.
A prosecution official said an arrest warrant for Kim Hyun-chul would be sought by the end of next week.
During parliamentary hearings this month on a loans-for-kickbacks scandal, opposition lawmakers accused the junior Kim of peddling influence to keep loans rolling to failed Hanbo Steel Co.
A prosecution spokesman told reporters on Tuesday an investigation found no evidence of wrongdoing linking Kim Hyun-chul to the collapse in January of Hanbo Steel under $5.8 billion in debts.
Prosecutors have been probing rumours that Kim Hyun-chul pocketed 200 billion won through Park acting as an agent for Hanbo.
Park, who has been grilled by prosecutors since Monday, has denied accusations by opposition politicians that he acted as a bagman for bribes from various companies on behalf of Kim Hyun-chul.
But a senior prosecutor said the prosecution had secured evidence implicating Kim Hyun-chul in offences unrelated to Hanbo.

The collapse of South Korea's second largest steelmaker uncovered a sleazy alliance between politicians and businessmen, tarnishing the politicial credibility of President Kim who took office with a pledge to stamp out corruption.
Eleven people, including ruling and opposition party lawmakers, top aides to President Kim, bankers and Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo are on trial for bribery.

In tearful testimony to parliament on Friday, Kim Hyun-chul begged for forgiveness for hurting his father but denied any wrongdoing. Opinion polls indicate most Koreans do not believe him and want legal action.

During the testimony, the junior Kim also countered charges by opposition politicians that he meddled in state affairs, including key appointments, and schemed with the help of the intelligence agencies. ($1 = 892.1 won)
